name: add_annotation
description: Attach a human-style ground-truth label (pass/fail + optional critique) to a trace or session, optionally as a golden label and optionally tied to a failure mode/cluster. Writes to the ground_truth_labels store; re-labeling the same target supersedes the prior label. Use to record verdicts an agent has judged.

name: add_to_dataset
description: Add traces/sessions to an existing dataset (by id or name). Returns how many were added vs skipped (duplicates). Use to grow a curated dataset over time.

name: cancel_preprod_run
description: Cancel a pre-prod run that is still awaiting traces or running. Terminal (a run that already completed/failed/cancelled) is refused rather than rewritten — cancelling is not a way to discard a result.

name: compare_preprod_runs
description: Line up TWO OR MORE pre-prod runs against each other over the same frozen golden version: per-run pass rate, average score and cost/latency/step traits, plus a matrix keyed by golden prompt with one cell per run. Name one run as baseline_run_id and each row also reports which runs REGRESSED against it. Every run must snapshot the same dataset version (list_preprod_runs shows it) — otherwise the request is refused rather than aligned on mismatched prompts.

run_ids.description: Two or more pre-prod run ids sharing one dataset version (required, max 25).

baseline_run_id.description: One of run_ids, to mark per-row regressions.

name: create_dataset
description: Create a dataset in the current project. If session_ids/trace_ids are given, the dataset is created AND populated from that selection (optionally as an immutable golden v1 via `golden`); otherwise an empty manual dataset is created. Datasets are a Silver+ tier feature. Use to curate failing traces for evaluation.

name: create_golden_version
description: Snapshot a dataset's CURRENT items into a new immutable version and mark it golden (pass golden:false for a plain snapshot). One golden version per dataset — goldening a new one un-goldens the previous. This is the step between curating a dataset and running a pre-prod eval or a model sweep against it, both of which replay a frozen version so results stay comparable.

golden.description: Mark it the dataset's golden version (default true).

name: create_judge
description: Create an LLM-prompt judge (scorer) in the project. Provide a prompt_template (use {target} for the trace/session), optional criteria, and required_data (input/output/messages/context/expected_output/metadata). Creates the judge + version 1 (experimental). Follow with deploy_judge then run_eval to score traces.

required_data.description: Data to feed the judge (default input/output/messages/metadata).

name: create_preprod_run
description: Create a pre-prod evaluation run over a dataset's frozen golden version at a candidate `version_label` (the branch/commit/deploy under test). It is created in `awaiting_traces` and runs NOTHING until start_preprod_run. runner_mode 'push' means Neens calls your endpoint itself and REQUIRES agent_connection_id; 'runner' (the default) means Neens waits for your own harness's traces. Gate it with min_pass_rate / max_regressions. Use run_verification instead when you are proving one specific remediation's fix.

dataset_id.description: Dataset id or name whose golden version is replayed (required).

dataset_version_id.description: Explicit frozen version instead of golden.

agent_connection_id.description: Registered agent_http connection; REQUIRED for runner_mode 'push'.

judge_deployment_ids.description: Graders (default: the project's scoreable deployed judges).

baseline_kind.description: What to compare against (default: 7d prod window).

baseline_run_id.description: The prior run, for baseline_kind preprod_run.

baseline_range.description: Window for a prod_window baseline, e.g. 7d.

name: deploy_judge
description: Deploy (enable) a judge version so it can run. Only the judge id is required: OMIT version_id to deploy the judge's LATEST version, or pass either a version id (list_judges → versions[].id / latestVersionId, or create_judge's latestVersionId) or a version NUMBER like "2". Never guess a version id — if it cannot be resolved the tool answers with the judge's real version ids. Re-deploying a version already enabled with the same trigger AND pass cutoff returns the existing deployment instead of a duplicate; changing either is a real, separate deployment. trigger_policy 'manual' scores on demand; 'on_new_trace' scores every new trace. The reply carries resolvedVersionId and the deployment id run_eval needs.

version_id.description: OPTIONAL. A judge version id, or a version number like "2". Omit to deploy the latest version.

name: export_dataset
description: Export a dataset — returned as a MANIFEST, never as the file: exact row count, row schema, a sha256 checksum of the full body, its byte size, and a 3-row head sample, plus the URL to GET the whole export (json or csv) over plain HTTP with the same credential. `complete:false` means the sample is a head, not the data. Inlining a real export would exceed the tool-result cap and come back silently truncated but still parseable, so it is never inlined.

name: export_dataset_version
description: Export one immutable dataset VERSION as a manifest — same contract as export_dataset (row count, schema, sha256 checksum, head sample, retrieval URL; never the inlined body), plus which version it is and whether it is golden. Use to hand a frozen evaluation set to another system by reference.

name: generate_remediation
description: Generate a grounded remediation (suggested fix) for a failure cluster or failure mode. Provide cluster_id or failure_mode_id. The generator classifies the failure locus from real evidence (error strings, HTTP status, span kind/status), so it may return an agent-fixable fix (prompt/tool change), an ADVISORY for a downstream/upstream service failure (naming the owning service, not a prompt edit), a working_as_intended note when a guardrail fired correctly, or a needs_grounding item held out of the actionable backlog until it is concrete and confident. Degrades deterministically when no LLM connection is configured. Use to propose a fix for a diagnosed failure.

name: get_business_kpis
description: List the project's Business KPIs (a measure promoted to a committed target) with current value, whether the target is met, and the recent trend. Pass kpi_id to drill into one KPI, including the failure clusters eroding it. A null value reads targetStatus 'unknown' (never 'missed'). Use for 'how are our KPIs doing', 'are we hitting our targets', or 'what's dragging KPI X down'.

kpi_id.description: Drill into one KPI by id (from a prior list). Omit to list all.

range.description: Time window token, e.g. 7d / 30d (default the server default).

name: get_cluster_exemplars
description: The most REPRESENTATIVE traces of a cluster — the members nearest its centroid, with their distance. A short read to understand what a failure mode looks like before pulling the whole set with list_traces(cluster_id=…).

name: get_current_project
description: Report which project THIS connection is scoped to — its name, id, org and company — plus how the scope was set (credentialKind, scopePinned) and your role. A project API key and an SSO/OAuth MCP token each pin one project, so this is the answer to 'which project am I connected to?'. Call it FIRST in a session to confirm the project (e.g. after an SSO sign-in) before reading or writing. Returns projectId=null with a note when no single project is pinned (a user session picks its active project per request).

name: get_dataset_items
description: Read a dataset's LIVE items (input, expected output, captured output, source trace). Optional text search `q` and `kind` filter. `total` is how many items the dataset has and `returned` how many came back — `complete: false` means you are looking at a page, not the set.

name: get_dataset_version_items
description: Read one immutable version's frozen snapshot items. Same shape as get_dataset_items but for a version, so it never changes under a run. `version` is the integer version NUMBER from list_dataset_versions, not the version id.

name: get_eval_run
description: Open one evaluation run by id: status, per-status task counts, success rate, and a page of its scored TASKS (target id, score, label, reason, error). `taskTotal` is the run's whole size; `tasks` is at most `limit` rows from `offset`. Use after run_eval to see what a judge actually decided, per trace.

name: get_failure_mode
description: Fetch one failure cluster/mode by id: label, description, root cause, remediation summary, and member session ids. Use after list_failure_modes to drill into a specific mode.

name: get_fix_bundle
description: Fetch a remediation's FIX BUNDLE. For an ACTIONABLE fix this is the paste-ready markdown brief (root cause + typed before/after fix spec + redacted failing exemplars), the pre-generated `neens eval run` CI command, the gate policy, the proof evals, and the acceptance criteria — everything a coding agent needs to implement the fix. The reply also carries failureLocus / actionability / owningComponent: when actionability is `advisory` the bundle is NOT a prompt fix — it describes a downstream/upstream service failure, names the owning service, and recommends a resilience/ownership action rather than an agent edit. Requires remediation_id (from list_open_remediations).

name: get_fix_run
description: Poll a fix run by id for its status (queued|applying|verifying|pr_opened|failed|drafted|cancelled), attempt count, pass^k eval report, verifying judges, the opened PR url, and the failure report if it could not be verified. Use to check a run started by start_fix_run.

name: get_judge_runs
description: List the eval runs of ONE judge, newest first: status, targets scored, average score and pass rate per run, plus an active/historic summary. Use to find the run id to open with get_eval_run, or to see whether a judge has ever scored.

name: get_model_sweep
description: Poll a model sweep by id: its status (queued|running|completed|completed_with_failures|failed|cancelled|void), the pinned conditions, the cost estimate, and a PER-ARM summary — model, status, pass^k as greens/k, and terminal vs total runs. Partial results are normal: read the per-arm status rather than waiting for the whole sweep. Two honesty rules to respect when reporting: a status of `void` means the arms did NOT run under identical conditions, so the arms are NOT comparable and voidReason says why — never rank them; and an estimate with partial=true excludes the unpriced models it names, so its totalUsd is a floor, not the cost.

name: get_model_sweep_comparison
description: DECIDE a model sweep: the N-way comparison of its arms and the answer — which model to ship. Returns one verdict sentence plus a per-arm leaderboard (pass rate WITH its sample size n and a 95% confidence interval, pass^k greens/k, p95 latency, cost per case, regressions vs the declared baseline arm) and a verdict PER AGENT, because the answer legitimately differs by agent. Four rules to respect when reporting the result: (1) comparable=false means the sweep is VOID — its arms did not run under identical conditions, so never rank them, whatever their numbers say; (2) costPerCaseUsd=null means UNPRICED, never free — such an arm cannot win 'cheapest' and appears in verdict.excluded with reasonCode 'unpriced'; (3) rate=null means no data, not 0%; (4) an item counts as passed only when it passed EVERY repeat run — 2 of 3 is not a pass, and flakyItems counts the difference. Read-only: computes nothing new and spends nothing.

bar.description: Pass-rate bar in 0-1 to decide against. Default: the sweep's pinned gate min_pass_rate, else the deployment's success threshold. The response's bar.source says which was used.

baseline_arm.description: Arm id to compare against. Default: the DECLARED incumbent (position 0) — never the best performer, since a baseline picked after seeing the results is not a baseline.

name: get_preprod_comparison
description: The candidate-vs-BASELINE verdict for one pre-prod run: the candidate's pass rate, the REGRESSION set (baseline passed, candidate failed), the new passes, and cost/latency/step deltas. The baseline is the run's own — a prior run or a prod window — and `baseline` overrides which. Two reporting rules: read `regressionCount`, not the length of the capped `regressions` evidence list; and a null passRate or null cost delta means NO DATA (nothing scored, nothing priced), never zero.

baseline.description: Override the run's stored baseline kind.

name: get_preprod_metrics
description: PER-METRIC score rollup for one pre-prod run — average and pass rate grouped by metric key. This is the CI-gate surface: it enforces 'faithfulness must stay ≥ 0.8' where the run's single aggregate pass rate cannot. `scored: 0` on a run that has captured nothing is an honest answer, not an error.

name: get_preprod_run_items
description: The run's FROZEN prompt list: one row per golden item with its `itemId`, input and expected output. The itemId is the stable id a harness stamps as `neens.dataset_item_id`, and the `item_id` get_preprod_trajectory diffs on.

name: get_preprod_trajectory
description: Diff HOW the agent behaved on ONE golden prompt between a candidate and a baseline pre-prod run: each run's captured trajectory reduced to an ordered tool-call/LLM step list, LCS-aligned, with added/removed/changed steps. Use after get_preprod_comparison to explain WHY an item regressed. A null sessionId means that run captured nothing for the prompt, so its side of the diff is empty — which is not the same as 'no change'.

name: get_prompt_optimization
description: Poll a prompt-optimization run by id: status (queued|running|completed|failed|cancelled), the baseline vs best HELD-OUT score and the improvement, rollouts and iterations spent, the candidate lineage with Pareto/winner flags, the verdict, the markdown proof report, and the emitted remediation id when the winner cleared the bar. A run that never beat baseline completes with emit=false — a legitimate result, not an error.

name: get_remediation
description: Fetch one remediation by id with its simulations and what-changed correlation. The reply carries the grounded-flow evidence: failureLocus (where the failure lives), actionability (`actionable` = agent-fixable, `advisory` = a downstream/upstream service issue owned by owningComponent, not a prompt fix), groundingStatus (needs_grounding items are not yet concrete/confident), rootCauseSignature (the dedup key), fixability, and a likelyCause synthesized from the dominant error signature. Use to review a fix's evidence before accepting/applying it — and note that moving it to applied/verified requires a bound proof (see update_remediation).

name: get_trace
description: Fetch one trace (session) by id: agent, status, timing, cost, error, and a summary of its spans and tool calls. Use to inspect a specific trace before annotating it or diagnosing a failure.

name: get_verification_run
description: Poll a verification (pre-prod) run by id for its proven verdict: status, whether it passed the gate, the failure reasons, regressions, pass rate, and score aggregate. Use to check a run started by run_verification that hadn't finished yet.

name: list_clusters
description: List the ACTIVE failure clusters from the latest clustering run — id, label, description, session count and L1 bucket. The id is what list_traces takes as `cluster_id` to get that cluster's exact traces. Use this rather than matching a cluster's name. (list_failure_modes is the richer hero view of the same run, with readiness and root-cause hypotheses.)

name: list_dataset_versions
description: List a dataset's immutable VERSIONS (snapshots), newest first, and name which one is golden. A pre-prod run and a model sweep both replay a frozen version, and create_preprod_run resolves the GOLDEN one when you give it no version — so check here first if a run refuses with 'dataset has no golden version'.

name: list_datasets
description: List the project's datasets: id, name, item count, source kind, tags and the cluster a from-cluster dataset was built from. Use to find an existing dataset before creating one, or to get the id the version/export/pre-prod tools take.

name: list_failure_modes
description: Summarize the latest failure-clustering run: readiness, top failure modes (label, description, session counts, NEW flags, root-cause hypotheses). Use to understand what's failing before generating a remediation or a judge.

name: list_judges
description: List the project's judges (scorers) with their versions and DEPLOYMENTS. Each deployment carries the `id` that run_eval and create_preprod_run need, plus its trigger, status and last run — so picking a judge to score with takes one call. Use before run_eval, or to find an existing judge instead of creating a duplicate. (list_scores is different: it reports how each METRIC is trending.)

name: list_open_remediations
description: List the OPEN backlog of AGENT-FIXABLE remediations, ranked by priority. By default this is only what a coding agent can actually implement and prove: status proposed/accepted, grounded (a concrete, confident fix), and actionable (agent_reasoning / tool_contract / quality). It EXCLUDES verified/closed + archived items (include_resolved=true), advisory items — downstream/upstream service failures that name a service owner, not a prompt fix (include_advisories=true), and needs_grounding items held back until concrete+confident (include_ungrounded=true). Each row carries failureLocus, actionability, owningComponent (for advisories), its lifecycle status, any PR/commit reported, and the last verification run id. Use this to find the next fix to implement + prove.

include_advisories.description: Also include advisory (infra/downstream/upstream) items that name a service owner rather than an agent-fixable change. Default false.

include_ungrounded.description: Also include needs_grounding items held out of the backlog until they are concrete and confident. Default false.

name: list_preprod_runs
description: List the project's pre-prod eval runs, newest first: status, version label, dataset + FROZEN dataset version id, gate, progress and regression count. The datasetVersionId is what tells you which runs are comparable — compare_preprod_runs requires runs that share one. Filter by status or dataset_id.

status.description: awaiting_traces | running | completed | completed_with_regressions | failed | cancelled.

name: list_remediations
description: List suggested fixes (remediations) ranked by priority, with a stats rollup. Filter by status, workState, clusterId, failureModeId, or type. Each row carries failureLocus (where the failure lives) and actionability: `actionable` items are agent-fixable in-repo, `advisory` items are downstream/upstream service failures that name an owningComponent instead of a prompt fix, and non_actionable covers working-as-intended controls; groundingStatus flags items held as needs_grounding until concrete+confident. Use to see the full backlog before transitioning a remediation's lifecycle. (For only the agent-fixable open backlog, use list_open_remediations.)

status.description: proposed | accepted | applied | verified | closed | regressed.

name: list_score_rows
description: List INDIVIDUAL score rows — one per scored trace/session — with the judge's score, label and reason, filterable by metric_key, pass/fail `status`, score range, target, source or a specific eval `run_id`. This is the per-row read; list_scores is the aggregate rollup. Use to find WHICH traces a judge failed. `run_id` reads that run's own snapshot and cannot be combined with metric_key, source or range — that branch applies none of them, so it is refused rather than answered with unfiltered rows.

status.description: Compared against each row's own threshold.

run_id.description: Restrict to one eval run's own snapshot. Mutually exclusive with metric_key / source / range.

lifecycle.description: Default finalized — experimental judges are hidden.

sort.description: Default latest. 'lowest' surfaces the worst first.

name: list_scores
description: List the score types / scorers active in the project and how each is trending: metric key, label, source, target type, average, scored count, pass rate, and period-over-period delta. Use to see eval coverage and quality trends.

name: list_traces
description: List/search agent traces (sessions) in the current project. Filter by status, agent, FAILURE CLUSTER (`cluster_id` — the exact membership set, from list_clusters / list_failure_modes), score metric/label/status, issue mode, failure set, model, tool name, tags, source, free text, time bounds, conversation, and duration/token ranges. Returns the total match count and up to `limit` summary rows. Use to find traces to inspect, annotate, or add to a dataset.

cluster_id.description: Failure-cluster id (from list_clusters / list_failure_modes) — the exact membership set, never a name match. Prefer this over issue_mode.

score_status.description: pass | fail — use together with score_metric.

score_label.description: Exact score LABEL, e.g. a classifier's class name.

failure_set.description: Restrict to the clustering failure set.

model.description: Model names; repeatable (OR within the filter).

tool_name.description: Tool names the trace called; repeatable (OR).

started_after.description: ISO 8601 lower bound on trace start time.

started_before.description: ISO 8601 upper bound on trace start time.

name: record_fix_merge
description: Tell Neens a fix PR was MERGED so it can start a post-merge efficacy close-out: Neens stamps a deploy event + a close-out watch and, after the post-deploy window, measures the fixed failure mode's real production volume before vs after and auto-verifies (or flags a regression of) the remediation. remediation_id is required; pr_url/commit_sha default from the remediation, merged_at defaults to now.

pr_url.description: The merged PR url (else the remediation's).

name: regenerate_remediation
description: Regenerate a remediation with the current engine, archiving the prior one as a superseded predecessor; returns the fresh remediation. Use after the detection/remediation engine has changed, or new failing traces have arrived, to re-run the current grounded engine for the same failure source (cluster or failure mode). The old proposal is preserved (archived + superseded, restorable) — nothing is deleted, and its PR/verification state is kept. The reply carries regeneratedFromId (the archived predecessor).

name: report_fix_status
description: Report a fix's progress back to Neens: set the remediation's lifecycle `status` (proposed|accepted|applied|verified|closed|regressed) and/or `work_state` (todo|in_progress|done|archived), and record the `pr_url` + `commit_sha` where the fix landed. remediation_id + at least one other field required. Use after opening a PR or applying a fix so the loop is auditable.

pr_url.description: The PR the fix was opened in (http/https).

commit_sha.description: The commit the fix landed on.

name: run_eval
description: Start an evaluation run for a deployed judge. Pass deployment_id (list_judges → deployments[].id, or deploy_judge's reply) OR just judge_id, in which case that judge's single enabled deployment is used — if it has none, or more than one, the tool says so and names the candidates. Never guess a deployment id. Scores the deployment's targeted traces and writes scores. By default the DEPLOYMENT's sampling filter decides how many traces a run covers; pass sample_size to cap THIS run at that many of the deployment's eligible traces (most-recent first) without editing the deployment — e.g. sample_size=1000 to score 1000 traces. Returns the run id, status, resolvedDeploymentId and total (the number actually queued, which is smaller than sample_size when fewer traces are eligible).

deployment_id.description: Judge deployment id. Omit it and pass judge_id to use the judge's enabled deployment.

judge_id.description: Judge id — resolves that judge's enabled deployment when deployment_id is omitted.

sample_size.description: Cap THIS run at this many of the deployment's eligible traces (most-recent first), leaving the deployment's sampling filter unchanged. Omit to let the deployment decide the count.

name: run_verification
description: PROVE a fix works: trigger a REAL pre-prod PUSH evaluation that calls the given candidate endpoint (endpoint_url — a preview deployment/branch — or an existing agent_connection_id) with the remediation's golden dataset, scores every response with the proof judges, and gates on regressions vs the baseline. version_label (the branch/commit/preview id) is required. Pass remediation_id to derive the golden dataset from its proof gate and stamp the result back onto the fix. Polls up to wait_seconds for a verdict and returns proven pass/fail + pass rate + regressions; if still running, returns the runId to poll with get_verification_run. This is the differentiator — a real eval against your branch, not a guess.

remediation_id.description: Ties the run to a fix + derives its golden dataset.

endpoint_url.description: Preview deployment base URL to PUSH-eval.

agent_connection_id.description: OR an existing agent_http connection id.

auth_token.description: Optional bearer token for endpoint_url (stored encrypted).

dataset_id.description: Explicit golden dataset (else derived from remediation).

wait_seconds.description: How long to poll for a verdict (default 90, max 300).

name: start_fix_run
description: Launch a Neens-ORCHESTRATED, eval-verified fix run for an accepted remediation: Neens proposes a patch from the fix bundle, applies it on a branch, VERIFIES it with pass^k pre-prod runs against the remediation's failure-derived evals + the regression set, and ONLY if green opens a PR (a human still merges). Requires remediation_id (with a resolvable proof-gate dataset). Returns the queued/terminal fix-run — poll it with get_fix_run. Optional: driver, vcs_installation_id, endpoint_url, version_label, pass_k, max_attempts.

vcs_installation_id.description: VCS installation to open the PR against.

endpoint_url.description: Preview deploy URL to PUSH-verify against.

agent_connection_id.description: OR an existing agent_http connection id.

name: start_model_sweep
description: Launch a MULTI-MODEL SWEEP: replay ONE frozen golden dataset version against N candidate model arms, k times each, and report pass^k PER ARM — the evidence for 'which model should we ship'. Every arm runs under IDENTICAL conditions (same frozen items, same judges, same k, same gate); only the agent connection (and so the model) differs. Requires name, version_label, and arms — an array of {label, agent_connection_id} naming a registered agent_http connection per model. Give dataset_id (its golden version is used), dataset_version_id, or scenario_suite_id. Cost is bounded: the sweep is refused if it exceeds budget_usd or the deployment's arm/k/run ceilings. Returns the queued sweep — poll it with get_model_sweep. Preview the cost first with POST /model-sweeps/preview if you want an estimate before spending.

version_label.description: Candidate version label — the branch/commit/deploy every arm is evaluated at (required).

arms.description: One entry per model under comparison (required). Two arms pointing at the SAME connection is not a comparison and is rejected.

label.description: Display name for the arm, e.g. 'sonnet'.

agent_connection_id.description: Id of a registered agent_http connection whose endpoint runs that model.

dataset_id.description: Golden dataset to replay (its frozen golden version is snapshotted).

scenario_suite_id.description: Or a ready synthetic scenario suite, whose frozen version is used.

pass_k.description: Repeat runs per arm (default per config, clamped to the deployment cap). k>1 is what defeats a flaky green.

judge_deployment_ids.description: Graders (default: the project's deployed judges). Pinned once, reused by every arm.

budget_usd.description: Refuse to launch if the pre-flight estimate exceeds this.

name: start_preprod_run
description: Start a created pre-prod run. Routes itself: a 'push' run is executed by Neens against its agent endpoint, a 'runner' run is moved to `running` to await your harness's traces — the tool reads the run's own runner_mode, so you do not have to pick. Refuses a run that is already terminal. Under an inline queue the returned run may already be finished; otherwise poll it with list_preprod_runs or read the verdict with get_preprod_comparison.

mode.description: Override the run's own runner_mode (rarely needed).

name: start_prompt_optimization
description: Launch an OFFLINE, GEPA-style prompt-optimization run for a confirmed failure mode: Neens replays that mode's HISTORICAL traces under candidate system prompts (tool results served from each recorded trace — no live traffic), grades every rollout with the project's judges, reflects on the graded trajectories, and proves the winner on a held-out split. A winner that clears the bar is emitted as a normal prompt_change remediation you can then fix-run (start_fix_run) — it is a PROPOSAL, never a deploy. Requires failure_mode_id (preferred), cluster_id, or session_ids. Returns the queued/terminal run — poll it with get_prompt_optimization.

failure_mode_id.description: Seed failure mode (preferred — its eval gate becomes the emitted fix's proof gate).

objective.description: Free-text steer for the reflection step.

max_rollouts.description: Rollout budget (clamped to the deployment cap).

name: update_remediation
description: Transition a remediation's lifecycle: `status` (proof lane: proposed|accepted|applied|verified|closed|regressed) and/or `work_state` (triage lane: todo|in_progress|done|archived) and/or `labels`. At least one required. Use to accept, progress, or archive a fix. Moving an ACTIONABLE fix to `applied` or `verified` now requires a bound proof — a verification run (run_verification) or a bound eval gate — or an explicit force override with a reason; without one the transition is refused. Advisory / working_as_intended items have no agent eval and settle as `closed` with an acknowledgement note instead. (Deleting remediations requires an admin over HTTP — not exposed here.)
